newsitem.title: POLAND: POLISH FUEL DISTRIBUTOR WORKERS TO STRIKE FEB 12.
newsitem.headline: POLISH FUEL DISTRIBUTOR WORKERS TO STRIKE FEB 12.

text.p: Trade unions at Poland's largest fuel distribution firm Centrala Produktow Naftowych SA (CPN) went on strike readiness on Monday and called a two-hour warning strike for February 12, a trade union official said.

The unions, in a dispute with the government since October last year, are protesting against the way CPN is being privatised, which, they say, would involve the loss of 4,500 out of its current 14,000 jobs.

"If we are not invited to talks by the governemnt we will think of stepping up the protest, although we will certainly not paralyse CPN," PAP news agency quoted the coordinator of the national strike committee, Walenty Cywinski, as saying.

Under the government's oil-sector restructuring plan, CPN, which accounts for 1,300 out of the country's 4,700 petrol stations, will be divided into three firms in charge of petrol storage, transport and filling stations.
Shares in he companies would be handed over to the state-owned oil holding Nafta Polska SA, which would eventually sell them to investors.

The unions also say the division of CPN into three firms would substantially lower the value of the shares they, as employees of a privatised company, would receive for free in accordance with Poland's new privatisation law.
